This tier has a real (file://) remote, an enabled ledger with intents published on several
branches, and a second capability repository. Network is left ENABLED, because the property
under test is that a read path does not use it.

topology.remoteBranchesNote: Three work branches carrying intents, plus the ledger's own state branch.

note: A budget cannot express this. Time budgets are met by a fast network and blown by a slow
one, which is why the read path was allowed to fetch for as long as it did -- nothing was
asserting that it must not. This counts network subprocesses via
SINGULARITY_FLOW_SUBPROCESS_PROBE and is machine-independent: zero is zero on any runner.
A read answers questions and must not change the repository. The ledger's read queries
each built a temporary worktree to read a few JSON files, so a snapshot wrote an entry
under .git/worktrees, took the index lock, and created a branch it then deleted. An
interrupted read left that behind; two concurrent reads contended for the lock.
